profiles.name: MiniMax H3 audio + video
profiles.description: Offline MiniMax-H3 generation through audio.cpp release-0.6. The Yeti profile is tuned for a 12 GB RTX 4070: Q4_K, memory saver, layerwise weights, short 480p video, and audio-first defaults.
requirements: audio.cpp release-0.6 audiocpp_cli built with CUDA
MiniMax-H3-Q4-GGUF package in L3MS_MEDIA_ROOT
NVIDIA driver/toolkit compatible with the audio.cpp CUDA build
notes: The normal Q4_K DiT is the default; the optional INT8 ConvRot package is not selected because audio.cpp reports a higher peak-memory path.
Video defaults to 480p and 121 frames (about five seconds at 24 fps). Use --video to request synchronized video output.
When ffmpeg, jq, and xxd are available, --video also muxes the RGB24 payload with the generated WAV into a playable MP4; the raw JSON artifact is retained.
H3 is experimental and can be slow on 12 GB. Keep other GPU-heavy models unloaded while generating.

profiles.name: LTX-2.5 synchronized video
profiles.variant: 22B distilled, FP8-cast at load, CPU offload
profiles.description: Text-to-video/audio generation through the official LTX-2.5 DistilledPipeline. The official BF16 transformer is quantized to FP8 while loading and offloaded to CPU; an explicit transformer-path override is available for future compatible pre-quantized releases.
requirements: Lightricks/LTX-2 checkout with uv sync --extra natten
Hugging Face access to the gated LTX-2.5 files
about 66 GiB of model storage plus CPU RAM and swap
notes: The official LTX-2.5 repository currently publishes BF16 split components; no official pre-quantized Ada transformer is listed. The selected fp8-cast policy still stores the eligible transformer linears in FP8 during inference.
The newly reported 2.5 NVFP4 transformer is a Blackwell-oriented path and is about 18.7 GB before runtime overhead, so it is not selected for this 12 GB Ada host.
The convolutional video VAE is selected to avoid requiring the diffusion VAE attention extra during decode.
Use --transformer PATH with the matching --quantization policy only after a pre-quantized artifact has been verified against the official ltx-pipelines loader.
The distilled pipeline accepts still-image conditioning through --image PATH FRAME STRENGTH. Use a dedicated LTX pipeline for audio-to-video or video-to-video inputs.

profiles.name: YuE2 foundation music generation
profiles.variant: 3B BF16 / FP8 AR, flow matching NAR, YuE2-Vae 48kHz stereo
profiles.description: Offline prompt-, lyrics-, and score-conditioned full-song generation through the official YuE2 pipeline with FP8 and memory budget tuning for 12 GB GPUs.
requirements: YuE repository checkout with Python 3.12 uv virtual environment (yue2-infer)
YuE2-3B and YuE2-Vae models in L3MS_MEDIA_ROOT/YuE2 or Hugging Face cache
NVIDIA GPU with CUDA and BF16 support (FP8 supported on Ada Lovelace / CC >= 8.9)
notes: YuE2 generates an editable ABC melody-and-chord plan, predicts semantic tokens, synthesizes acoustic latents, and decodes 48 kHz stereo audio.
Supports --cot {full,melody,off}, --abc-file for exact-score conditioning, --quantization {none,fp8}, and --budget GiB.
On 12 GB GPUs like Yeti's RTX 4070, --quantization fp8 and --budget 12 are recommended defaults.
Keep llama-swap GPU models unloaded during generation.

profiles.name: HeartMuLa local music generation
profiles.description: Offline prompt-, tag-, and lyrics-conditioned song generation through audio.cpp using its published HeartMuLa Q8_0 GGUF package.
requirements: audio.cpp release-0.6 audiocpp_cli built with HeartMuLa and CUDA
HeartMuLa Q8_0 GGUF package in L3MS_MEDIA_ROOT
NVIDIA driver/toolkit compatible with the audio.cpp CUDA build
notes: The Q8_0 package is audio.cpp's recommended HeartMuLa download and contains the MuLa generator and HeartCodec assets in one GGUF.
Use --instrumental for a no-vocals tag preset or --lyrics/--lyrics-file for a supplied lyric sheet.
Memory saver is enabled for the 12 GB Yeti profile; keep llama-swap GPU models unloaded during generation.

profiles.name: Breeze-TTS-2 speech generation & voice cloning
profiles.variant: Breeze-TTS-2 Q8_0 GGUF, CUDA, T5Gemma conditioning + Mimi codec
profiles.description: Native audio.cpp Breeze-TTS-2 Q8_0 speech generation with standard TTS, instruction-led voice design, reference-audio cloning, offline output, and incremental streaming.
requirements: audio.cpp audiocpp_cli built with breeze_tts and CUDA
Breeze-TTS-2 Q8_0 GGUF package and breeze_tts model spec available locally
NVIDIA driver/toolkit compatible with the audio.cpp CUDA build
notes: Default Q8_0 package contains T5Gemma text conditioning, Qwen-style acoustic code generation, depth codebook decoding, and Mimi waveform decoding.
Standard speech uses native --task tts; the wrapper's --task design alias also uses tts with an instruction prompt.
Voice cloning uses native --task clon and a reference WAV via --voice-ref; --reference-text is optional.
Offline mode writes one WAV; streaming mode emits audio chunks under <output>.chunks and retains the final WAV at --output.
Run media-models/generate-breeze-tts-2.sh --check for a read-only CLI/loader/model/spec preflight; it does not load the model or verify GPU capacity.
CUDA backend uses bf16 activation rounding by default for reference parity with official Breeze-TTS 2.

profiles.name: Breeze-TTS-2 CPU speech
profiles.variant: Breeze-TTS-2 Q8_0 GGUF, explicitly selected CPU backend
profiles.description: Explicit CPU standard, instructed voice-design and reference-audio cloning speech, with offline or chunked TTS output. No CUDA fallback; performance and quality require local acceptance.
requirements: audio.cpp audiocpp_cli with CPU backend and breeze_tts loader
Breeze-TTS-2 Q8_0 GGUF package and model spec available locally
notes: The standalone CPU profile passes --backend cpu; direct script calls must select it explicitly because the script default remains CUDA.
The direct wrapper requires a nonempty reference transcript for cloning. Standard TTS optionally writes streaming chunks, returned after completion rather than played live.

profiles.name: Blender 3D scene & mesh generation
profiles.variant: Blender 5.2.1 LTS, local socket MCP bridge (port 9876)
profiles.description: Interactive and headless 3D modeling, asset creation, material styling, and rendering in Blender 5.2.1 LTS via Model Context Protocol (blender-mcp) or direct Python execution.
requirements: Blender 5.2.1 LTS at ~/.local/bin/blender
blender_mcp addon installed and enabled in Blender user preferences
blender-mcp CLI server runner via uv tool / uvx
MCP client configured at ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json
notes: Interactive: in Blender 3D Viewport, press N -> MCP for Blender -> Start MCP Server (port 9876).
MCP integration supports live scene inspection, object creation/manipulation, shader nodes, and viewport capture.
Headless: script also supports direct background Python execution and image rendering without GUI.

profiles.name: Qwen Image 2.1 image generation
profiles.variant: INT8 ConvRot diffusion model and Qwen3-VL encoder, BF16 VAE
profiles.description: Text-to-image generation through the local ComfyUI API with the official quantized Qwen Image 2.1 weights. Bundled ComfyUI workflows also support image editing and transparent PNG output.
requirements: ComfyUI at the pinned Qwen Image 2.1-compatible revision
Official Qwen Image 2.1 ComfyUI files installed by maintenance/setup-qwen-image-2.1-comfyui.sh
Exclusive GPU time; stop llama-swap before starting ComfyUI in GPU mode
notes: The Yeti setup uses the official INT8 ConvRot model and text encoder with the BF16 VAE; the three files total about 16.1 GiB on disk.
The CLI default is 1024x1024, 25 steps, CFG 1, Euler/simple. Keep dimensions divisible by 32 and start at 1024 on the 12 GB RTX 4070.
Import workflows/qwen-image-2.1/image_qwen_image_2_1_t2i.json or image_qwen_image_2_1_image_edit.json for the full native ComfyUI workflow.

profiles.name: Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo image generation
profiles.variant: INT8 ConvRot Turbo diffusion model, Qwen3-VL encoder, BF16 VAE, 8 steps
profiles.description: Accelerated 8-step text-to-image generation through the local ComfyUI API using Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo INT8 ConvRot with official sampling sigmas.
requirements: ComfyUI at the pinned Qwen Image 2.1-compatible revision
Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo INT8 ConvRot files installed by maintenance/setup-qwen-image-2.1-turbo-comfyui.sh
Exclusive GPU time; stop llama-swap before starting ComfyUI in GPU mode
notes: Uses the INT8 ConvRot quantization of official Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo with shared Qwen3-VL INT8 text encoder and BF16 VAE.
The CLI default is 1024x1024, 8 Euler steps with the official schedule (1.0 -> 0.414568 -> 0.0), CFG 1.0, and seed 42.
Generates images ~3x faster than baseline 25-step Qwen Image 2.1 while fitting in 12 GB VRAM on Yeti.

profiles.name: Krea 2 raw int8 image generation
profiles.variant: INT8 ConvRot raw model with r128 Turbo distill LoRA (0.60 strength), Qwen3-VL 4B encoder, VAE
profiles.description: Text-to-image generation through the local ComfyUI API using Krea 2 raw int8 with the distilled Turbo LoRA (r128). Tuned for 12 GB GPUs at resolutions up to 1024x1536, 12 steps, and CFG 1.5.
requirements: ComfyUI at the pinned Krea 2-compatible revision
Official Krea 2 ComfyUI and Turbo LoRA files installed by maintenance/setup-krea-2-comfyui.sh
Exclusive GPU time; stop llama-swap before starting ComfyUI in GPU mode
notes: Uses the official INT8 ConvRot raw DiT model and Qwen3-VL 4B FP8 text encoder with the r128 distilled Turbo LoRA (strength 0.60, 12 steps, CFG 1.5).
The CLI default is 1024x1024 (or up to 1024x1536), 12 Euler/simple steps, and CFG 1.5. Keep dimensions divisible by 32 and resolutions <= 1024x1536 on 12 GiB GPUs.
Import workflows/krea-2/image_krea2_turbo_t2i_int8.json for native ComfyUI workflow usage.
